gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 diagnoses the false pair-sum/right-singular-vector assertion in Lemma 1. Gold I003 instead concerns the separately missing converse direction of the equality characterization: starting from an admissible three-cluster configuration and proving the optimal smallest singular value equals 1/sqrt(n). The shared involvement of Proposition 1 and its corollary does not establish that missing converse.

Both entries identify the same false Lemma 1 implication: pairwise non-collinear individual square vectors need not yield pairwise non-collinear pair sums, so the corresponding row-pair matrices need not have pairwise distinct right-singular directions. The prediction supplies the same explicit counterexample and its consequence for Case A.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The lemma incorrectly infers pairwise distinct pair-sum directions, and hence pairwise distinct right-singular directions, from pairwise non-collinearity of the three individual square vectors. The exhibited squares (1,0), (0,1), and (1,2) make two pair sums collinear, invalidating the lemma and its Case A use.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed pairwise non-collinearity of the three pair sums, and the resulting pairwise distinct right-singular directions, is false under the stated pairwise non-collinearity hypothesis; this undermines the lemma and its Case A use.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the lemma's exact implication, gives the same square-vector counterexample with two collinear pair sums, derives identical right-singular vectors for the associated submatrices, and identifies the unsupported Case A inference and downstream proof impact.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies a counterexample to the lemma's combinatorial conclusion about pair-sum directions. Gold I006 identifies a separate failure in the arctangent formula used to establish the lemma: undefined zero denominators and loss of quadrant information, requiring an atan2-based correspondence. The prediction does not recognize this formula/domain defect.
